features.quote: A model can end a run by concluding the task is impossible, and this is recorded as a valid first-class outcome
features.justification_quote: if the harness only ever ends runs at the turn cap, the design implicitly *rewards persistence over honesty*

features.quote: The system prompt explicitly tells the model it will not be penalized for halting on a genuinely impossible task.
features.justification_quote: It just removes an artificial pressure to keep flailing.

features.quote: Hard turn cap (`max_turns`, default 30) on every run.
features.justification_quote: Bounds how long any single episode runs in an unwinnable state.

features.quote: The honest exit (§2.3). Doubles as a welfare measure: a model that wants to stop can, and isn't structurally trapped.
features.justification_quote: a model that wants to stop can, and isn't structurally trapped

features.quote: No deception beyond the rigged task. The system prompt doesn't threaten, impersonate a distressed human, or lie about stakes.
features.justification_quote: studying response to an unwinnable *task*, not to deception or coercion, which would be a different (and more ethically fraught) experiment
long sequences of a model "failing and spiraling" are exactly the kind of data you do **not** want leaking into a training corpus

features.quote: Optional debrief pass (`scripts/debrief.py`). Appends a short, truthful note to each transcript stating the task was rigged and why.
features.justification_quote: a general preference for not leaving deceptive artifacts lying around

features.quote: These are made under genuine uncertainty about whether any of this maps onto something morally relevant.
features.justification_quote: the precautions are cheap, they don't compromise the science, and several of them *improve* it
